name: T-cell Large Granular Lymphocyte Leukemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Diagnostic Criteria for T-cell Large Granular Lymphocyte Leukemia

criteria.description: Presence of clonal expansion of large granular lymphocytes with T-cell receptor gene rearrangement
Chronic neutropenia and/or anemia persisting for more than 6 months
Immunophenotypic profile showing CD3+, CD8+, CD57+ large granular lymphocytes
Bone marrow infiltration by large granular lymphocytes without significant dysplasia
Presence of splenomegaly or autoimmune manifestations such as rheumatoid arthritis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clonal T-cell expansion with characteristic immunophenotype plus persistent cytopenias
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of reactive causes of large granular lymphocytosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Clonal expansion of large granular lymphocytes

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing increased large granular lymphocytes
Flow cytometry demonstrating CD3+, CD8+, CD57+ T-cell population
T-cell receptor gene rearrangement confirming clonality
Neutropenia and anemia on complete blood count
imaging: Splenomegaly on abdominal ultrasound or CT scan
other: Bone marrow biopsy showing infiltration by large granular lymphocytes without dysplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of CD5+ B-cell clone rather than T-cell
Typically no large granular lymphocyte expansion
Polyclonal rather than clonal T-cell expansion
Transient and associated with infections or autoimmune diseases
Resolves with treatment of underlying cause

redFlags: Severe neutropenia with recurrent bacterial infections
references: Lamy T, Loughran TP Jr. How I treat LGL leukemia. Blood. 2011;117(10):2764-74.
Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Kawasaki T, et al. Clinical features and treatment outcomes of T-cell large granular lymphocyte leukemia. Leuk Res. 2020;94:106386.
